q: Why is the terminal voltage of a battery smaller than its source voltage when a current is drawn from the battery?
a: The current also flows inside the battery, and in the internal resistance of the battery the potential drops by the voltage $R_\text{s} I$. So $U = E - R_\text{s} I$ is left between the terminals. Without a current the terminal voltage is the source voltage.

q: The source voltage of a battery is $9.0\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $1.8\,\Omega$. What is its short-circuit current, and why is a short circuit dangerous?
a: The short-circuit current is $I_\text{k} = E : R_\text{s} = 9.0\,\text{V} : 1.8\,\Omega = 5.0\,\text{A}$. Only the internal resistance limits the current, so the whole power of the source is changed into internal energy of the battery and the wire: they heat up, and the battery may leak or catch fire.
